observed: the 21-row list came from a sparse checker run (1509 scoped files scanned, 3844 not checked out): it missed 348 dependency rows, among them 8 in m3/release
correction: scan all 5353 scoped files (sparse patterns by suffix plus /.github/ and /m3/release/) before classifying
lesson: a sparse scan is not a repository claim: report unscanned and widen before deciding

observed: git ls-tree -l in a blobless clone reads every blob header, lazily fetched blobs one at a time and started git maintenance/gc in the repository
correction: ls-tree without -l; sizes and presence from git --no-lazy-fetch cat-file --batch-check; one batch fetch --stdin of the absent oids (2837 blobs, 5 MB, 3 s)
guard: stopped the runaway processes; maintenance.auto=false and gc.auto=0 in the work repository
lesson: never read blob sizes or contents in a partial clone without --no-lazy-fetch; batch the fetch

observed: git worktree add would write a 25 MB index into the shared clone on H: (389 MB free, floor 350 MB; later 98 MB through other writers)
correction: a separate repository on C: borrowing the H: objects through objects/info/alternates; lazy fetches and the index land on C:
guard: H: not written by this leaf
lesson: put new git metadata where the space is; alternates keep the shared store read-only

observed: replay in a fresh scratch repository differed 19/19: the global core.autocrlf=true rewrote LF to CRLF
lineage assertions (provenance checks, receipt fields) fetch nothing but count as D_REPO_REF
correction: the donor identity lives once in LINEAGE_SOURCES.tsv and the consumers read it; applied to 4 rows (2 workflows, 1 verifier with 2 rows)
lesson: lineage is data: keep it in a ledger, not as literals in executable files

observed: secrets.M3_SYNEXIA_TOKEN (second-pass review DAG) is not matched by the checker's D_SECRET rule: \bSYNEXIA_ needs a word boundary
correction: the leaf's fetch guard matches secrets.(M3_)?SYNEXIA_; the job was moved out

observed: two workflows assert donor lineage but their bytes are pinned by binding JSON (authoring-source-binding.json, source-binding.json) and recipe fixtures
correction: HOLD; a change must come from the owning recipe with a new binding

observed: master 52fb81c4 has 474 poms with the m3-recipe-boot profile; #2213 retired 470 because its scan read /m3/**/pom.xml only; .m3/openrewrite-recipes, make/m3/recipes, src/utils/IdealGraphVisualizer and src/utils/LogCompilation remain
correction: re-run RETIRE_PROFILE v1 over every pom of the tree
lesson: scope a retire recipe by file pattern over the whole tree, not by one directory

observed: m3/backports/recipes/j485/WORKFLOW_VALIDATOR_RECEIVER.tsv has no field/value header; its workflow step refuses it on master as well
correction: not changed here (outside the leaf); the step logic is tested on a headed copy
lesson: the j485 owner adds the header line (the jep-493 receiver has it)

observed: M3_MAVEN_CONTROL_REACTOR was owned by the donor repository, so a release needed another repository
correction: gate owner and canonical_recipe.repository = hsoliwal/M3jdk21 (PRODUCT_REPOSITORY, MAVEN_GATE); tests name another repository only as the refused case
guard: test_release_admission.py 29 run plus the owner discriminator
lesson: a release gate owned elsewhere makes the product non-standalone; #2192's fixture test that expects the contract to name another repository needs its own fixture after both land

observed: three A3 workflows still fetched the donor although the export was absorbed on 2026-10-12 (m3/vendor/synexia, tooling/synexia-jdk-a3-recipes) and one of them used codeload, which answers 404 for the private donor
correction: repoint the consumers to the absorbed copy; keep the sha256 seal; bootstrap the source-built closure
lesson: after an absorb, find and repoint every consumer in the same leaf

observed: v1 took the after counts from the REMAINS rows: after-only findings, kinds only the after scan holds and findings at a moved path were neither counted nor listed (probe: no D_SECRET row, D_REPO_REF after=1 for 2)
correction: classify both scans with the same rules; after counts from the after scan; after findings left once the before findings of the same kind/path/text are matched (line order) become NEW rows; kinds = union
guard: test_after_only_findings_new_kinds_and_moved_paths_are_counted_and_listed (fails on v1); after-only unclassified finding refused
lesson: a before/after ledger counts each side from its own scan, never from the other side's matches

observed: only M3_MAVEN_CONTROL_REACTOR's owner was checked: gate_owners.get(ident, PRODUCT_REPOSITORY) accepted any other owner the contract listed (probe: release_ready=True with M3_FOUNDATION_TESTS delegated)
correction: contract.recipe_owner blocks when any gate_owners value is not PRODUCT_REPOSITORY; every gate receipt must name PRODUCT_REPOSITORY
lesson: check an ownership rule over the whole owner map, not one key

observed: c6bc67d said the README follows the contract, but three policy paragraphs and the control-reactor job, step and summary labels still made Synexia the recipe owner; check_standalone.py skips .md, so no count saw them
correction: rewrote m3/release/README.md (historical recipes, unresolved queue rows, naming recipe); renamed the three labels; OWNER_POLICY docs NEXT in SYNEXIA_REFS.md
lesson: a policy change edits every normative statement of it, docs included; docs need their own scan

observed: the A3 export was ABSORB/RESOLVED but only its sources were absorbed: its 7 unit tests ran in no workflow, were not vendored and no gate recorded the lost coverage
correction: vendored the 7 tests byte-identically (pre-#2236 seals), added rewrite-test, a second default-testCompile root and the surefire working directory to tooling/synexia-jdk-a3-recipes, sealed 16 files in m3-a3.yml and gave the module tests their own step there
lesson: an absorb carries the donor's tests with its sources, or records the lost coverage as HOLD

observed: at the pinned revision M3JdkA3RecipeExportTest#exportedConvergenceRecipeIsTheCanonicalFileLocalDag asserts a synexia tag that the sealed M3PureIntConvergenceRecipe never carried, so the donor's own export build fails the same way
correction: surefire-hold-excludes.txt holds that one method; test and recipe stay byte-identical (sealed)
lesson: run a sealed donor closure's tests at absorb time: a seal proves bytes, not passing tests

observed: surefire 3.2.5 refuses a method filter in <excludes>: Method filter prohibited in includes|excludes parameter
correction: excludesFile, which accepts Class#method filters since surefire 3.0.0-M6
guard: A3_EXPORT_TESTS: 29 -> 28 run, only the held method left out
